study.question: At fixed task-conditioned compressed-history architecture and enabled auxiliary context transfer, does the loss from coordinate centering arise chiefly from its forward representation, its full upstream normalizer derivative, or their interaction?
study.hypothesis: Observed: native centering with auxiliary adapter-context transfer loses0.0008227367 click AUC, while centering under the blocked gate gains0.0001441887; stopping the RMS scale derivative also loses quality. A provisional explanation is that the centered normalizer VJP disrupts useful shared-context learning beyond what forward mean removal explains. Replacing only that VJP with the incumbent uncentered VJP may rescue the centered representation; the reciprocal intervention may hurt even with uncentered values. This is a prospective mechanism diagnostic and possible optimization candidate, not a novelty claim or an established explanation.

study.proposed_difference: Define U(x)=x/sqrt(mean(x^2)+1e-4) and C(x)=(x-mean(x))/sqrt(mean((x-mean(x))^2)+1e-4) per sample/task over rank16. Independently choose F in{U,C} and B in{U,C}; implement stopgrad(F(x)) + (B(x)-stopgrad(B(x))). The parentheses make the subtracted forward values identical, yielding exact finite forward F(x), while the upstream VJP is J_B(x)^T g. Downstream interaction-output weights still differentiate using F(x). Evaluate all four F/B cells with auxiliary adapter-context transfer fixed on. Execute both reference normalizers and a zero-weight unused branch in every cell. No parameters, state, inputs, loss, host recipe or current-label access are added.
